item.title: Arsène Wenger not expected to stand for FIFA presidency
item.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development Arsene Wenger stands in the stadium prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League final soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «Arsène Wenger not expected to stand for FIFA presidency») Robert Michael/dpa Arsène Wenger has decided against standing for the FIFA presidency in a boost for current incumbent Gianni Infantino, the Press Association understands. Wenger was touted as a potential rival to Infantino, who has lost the confidence of European football’s governing body, UEFA, over the controversial plan to seek private investment in a World Cup company. The deadline for candidates to declare their intention to stand is Wednesday, November 18, but former Arsenal manager Wenger has informed UEFA he will not go head-to-head with Infantino, the Press Association understands. It was first stated by UEFA in August that work to identify a credible candidate to challenge Infantino had got under way and Wenger was encouraged to stand. A senior figure in European football told the Press Association they believe Wenger would be the only person who could beat Infantino and put football first. Even though Wenger is European, he has served as FIFA’s chief of global football development since 2019 and has the respect of the football world after his Premier League success, which was preceded by successful stints in his homeland of France and Japan. Wenger had also earned a strong command of respect in Africa for his development work within FIFA but, in a blow to UEFA, the 77-year-old will not stand. This move could cement Infantino’s position as president despite the fallout of plans to create a company titled FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would manage commercial interests of FIFA’s competitions including the men’s and women’s World Cups. A private investor group, led by a company founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, were proposed to hold a minority stake in FFE. However, Infantino had to abandon the plan days after it emerged publicly after it was rejected by UEFA along with the Asian confederation and CONCACAF. It is the latest controversy regarding Infantino, who faced scrutiny after FIFA’s disciplinary committee decided to suspend a ban imposed on US forward Folarin Balogun during this year's tournament. Trump later admitted he had personally called Infantino to review Balogun’s suspension, but FIFA’s president has of late consolidated support as he targets a fourth term in position and Wenger’s decision to not stand is welcome news for the 56-year-old ahead of the FIFA Congress next March. Infantino has pledged “unanimous” backing from the Confederation of African Football (CAF), while the Asian confederation has U-turned and will now support his presidency bid.

item.title: Why Marist football struggled in shut out by visiting Butler
item.description: Marist struggled to move the ball consistently and turned it over twice as the Red Foxes slipped out of any contention for the Pioneer Football League title with a 28-0 loss to Butler before 2,167 at Tenney Stadium in Poughkeepsie on Saturday, Nov. 14. Marist has dropped three of its past four, falling to 5-6 and 4-3 in the PFL. Butler (9-2) moved into a first-place tie with Dayton at 6-1. Butler has beaten Marist four consecutive times since 2021 and leads the all-time series 5-4. Butler is a physical team that lived up to its reputation for sturdy defense. The Red Foxes were 2-for-15 on third-down conversions and 1-for-5 on fourth down, leading to seven punts by Ethan Yuska (37.7 yards average). Quarterback Sonny Mannino (18-for-32, 138 yards) was picked off in the second quarter, after moving the ball down to the Butler 13, and again in the fourth. Mannino was also sacked six times, for 34 total yards. Butler got touchdown runs of 6 and 3 yards from Michael Dellumo in the second and third quarters, respectively, for a 14-0 lead - it was the second week in a row that Dellumo had a pair of scores. The second score was set up with a rare quick kick on third down, pushing Marist back to its own 2, and after stopping the Red Foxes on three plays Butler's Madden Beriault returned a punt to the 13. Gabe Passini capped an 11-play, 56-yard drive with a 1-yard TD run early in the fourth, and Desmin Jackson scored from 6 yards out 92 seconds later after Tristan Johnson picked off Mannino and returned it 42 yards. Marist was held to 52 total yards rushing and 141 passing. Isaiah Simmons had 10 carries for 36 yards. Lincoln Cardillo had five receptions for 32 yards, Reed Shumpert three for 48 and Zach Garmont three for 25. Kade Werner had nine tackles. Passini was 10-for-16 for 101 yards, adding 14 carries for 69 yards. Michael Dellumo had 12 carries for 46 and Desmin Jackson eight for 26. Jayden Norris had 2.5 sacks, Jackson Stratton had eight tackles and Andrew Lieske had the early interception for the Bulldogs. Butler has held eight foes under 87 yards rushing. Marist had scored in 13 consecutive games. The last time the Red Foxes were shut out was Nov. 1, 2025, at Saint Thomas (Minn.) by a 45-0 count. Butler shut out Franklin 52-0 on Sept. 12. Marist closes the season on Nov. 21 at Davidson. Butler will host Morehead State. Kickoff for both games is 1 p.m. Before the game, Marist honored 21 senior athletes and two managers. kmcmillan@th-record.com X / Twitter: @KenMcMillanTHR This article originally appeared on Times Herald-Record: Why Marist football struggled in shut out by visiting Butler

item.description: Ulster wing Rob Baloucoune (left) crossed twice in the first half for Ireland [Getty Images] Nations Championship Ireland (17) 43 Tries: O'Brien 2, Baloucoune 2, Kelleher, Porter, Timoney Cons: Prendergast 3, Frawley Fiji (15) 15 Tries: Tuisova, Yato Con: Volavola Pen: Volavola Ireland recovered from a sluggish first-half performance to wear down spirited Fiji and keep alive their hopes of topping the Nations Championship northern hemisphere table with a bonus-point win in Dublin. After thumping Argentina last week, Ireland failed to click in an unconvincing opening, with Tommy O'Brien's early try and a Robert Baloucoune double enough for a 17-15 lead. Fiji arrived in Dublin without a win in nine previous meetings against their hosts, and having been thrashed 54-17 by France last week. But they dreamed of a historic win after tries from Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato, and a Ben Volavola penalty, kept them firmly in the contest at the break. However, Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and O'Brien crossed as Andy Farrell's men scored 26 unanswered second-half points to deny the Pacific Islanders, who remain without a point in the competition. The result left Ireland one point off northern hemisphere leaders France before next week's mouthwatering tussle with world champions South Africa in Dublin. When these sides last met, in Dublin two years ago, Ireland scored four converted tries to effectively end the contest by half-time on their way to a 52-17 win. But this was anything but simple. Despite making seven changes from last week's victory over the Pumas and losing centre Jamie Osborne to an early injury, Ireland threatened to gallop into the distance in a hurry. The back three of Hansen, Baloucoune and O'Brien connected to put the latter in for an eighth-minute try - the wing atoning for an earlier knock-on. Gibson-Park, back in the starting line-up, thought he had added a second for Ireland, but the scrum-half lost control of the ball as he touched down. From there, Fiji decided to get moving and hit back quickly when mountainous centre Tuisova barged over the line after a piercing carry by Yato. Yato, who took over the captaincy from Tevita Ikanivere for Saturday's game, then touched down himself after winger Juta Wainiqolo surged through a hole in the home defence. Irish frustration deepened when Ryan Baird was stopped just short of the line but, after a superb Prendergast kick caused havoc in the Fijian defence, the fly-half put Baloucoune in after good work from the impressive Hansen. Fiji, playing with rising confidence, responded when prop Luke Tagi burst over, but Isoa Nasilasila was adjudged to have knocked the ball in the away side's line-out. item.title: Michigan Football 4-star defensive commit flips to elite SEC program
item.description: Zach Libby/Maize n Brew It’s just about that time of year. No, I’m not taking about the holiday season or when my seasonal depression kicks in — I’m talking about #FlipSZN on the recruiting trail. Unfortunately, today’s update doesn’t favor the Wolverines, as 2027 four-star defensive back Tavares Harrington has flipped his commitment from Michigan to Ole Miss. I can only imagine he saw the Wolverines’ defense give up nearly 300 passing yards to Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola and said, “Yeah, I’m good, fam.” BREAKING: Four-Star Safety Tavares Harrington has Flipped his Commitment from Michigan to Ole Miss, he tells me for @Rivals The 6’3 185 S had been Committed to the Wolverines since May “Shark business🦈🏡” https://t.co/C2BqkK3Z9D pic.twitter.com/KQMM6ZJTmj — Hayes Fawcett (@Hayesfawcett3) November 14, 2026 The 6-foot-3, 180-pound Chicago, Illinois native committed to Michigan back in May, following a visit for Michigan’s spring game. However, he took a visit to Ole Miss — one of the original runner-ups in his recruitment — the weekend of Nov. 7. Harrington was one of the early building blocks of Michigan’s 2027 class. He is ranked No. 151 overall, No. 9 at the safety position and No. 8 in Illinois on the Rivals Industry Rankings. He is a versatile prospect who was recruited to Michigan as a nickel/safety. The timing of all this is not great for Michigan, with the early signing period getting underway very soon. The program is kind of in disarray right now, too, as the Wolverines are coming off a 15-6 loss to Michigan State, offensive coordinator Jason Beck was fired, the team is (as of this writing) getting its ass kicked by Oregon, and there is plenty of uncertainty about the direction of the program. Harrington’s decision comes during a stretch when commits across the country are re-evaluating their options, and Michigan’s current struggles on the field make it harder to hang on to every pledge. Harrington’s departure leaves a hole in a secondary class that had been one of the strongest parts of Michigan’s 2027 haul. The Wolverines still hold commitments from four-star cornerbacks Blake Jenkins and Darius Johnson, as well as three-star legacy safety prospect Charles Woodson Jr. But losing a four-star recruit that the coaching staff prioritized from the very beginning of their time in Ann Arbor takes the class down a notch. There is also a Mount Carmel angle to monitor. Harrington comes from the same Chicago program as 2027 four-star wide receiver Quentin Burrell, who is still committed to Michigan. Will this affect what Burrell does during the early signing period? Considering Burrell committed before Harrington, it likely won’t have a major impact, but only time will tell. The bigger concern is whether this is the start of a trend. The early signing period opens Dec. 2, and Michigan has an offensive coordinator vacancy, an uncertain head coaching situation to some outside observers, and a lot of recruiting momentum to protect. item.title: White has 'exciting future' despite boos - Rice
item.description: Declan Rice joined Ben White at Arsenal after signing from West Ham in 2023 [Getty Images] Declan Rice has defended Arsenal team-mate Ben White after the defender was booed at Wembley during England's 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday. White, who came on as a substitute in the Nations League fixture, left the Three Lions' camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to return home for personal reasons. He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate's reign. White was also booed by some fans in March's 1-1 draw with Ukraine after returning to the squad under Thomas Tuchel. "The incident with Ben was over five years ago, I don't know why it is still a conversation to be honest," Rice told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Knowing Ben, knowing the character he is, he has totally moved on from all of that. "He always wears the shirt with pride and every time he puts on the shirt, he gives 100 percent. "It shows his character. It is not easy being booed coming on at Wembley, but to show his mental strength to play the game and to play well, like he did in the previous months, is a real testament to him." Rice also said that the players do not discuss the situation at all and that everybody has moved on, adding that White has "an exciting future ahead with this England squad". Before the game, White said that people did not know the "full story" behind his departure from Qatar but that he still backed his decision. Rice close to signing new Arsenal contract Rice has also confirmed that he is close to signing a new contract with Arsenal. BBC Sport first revealed the midfielder was set to sign a new long-term deal at Emirates Stadium on 7 October, and the 27-year-old, speaking before England's game against Spain on Sunday, said: "A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon and I'm extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and team-mates who put so much energy in to me." Rice's current deal expires in 2028 but the former West Ham star is now expected to extended his tenure in north London, having arrived from London Stadium in 2023 in a deal worth £105m. The midfielder's new contract will put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner. Rice has managed to avoid upheaval during his career and he believes that continuity has helped him to blossom. "I've been extremely lucky I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career. I always set myself targets, pushing for more," he said. item.title: How did Minnesota survive travel adventure to Penn State football?
item.description: STATE COLLEGE — This became a Penn State football day like no other. At least for visiting Minnesota Golden Gophers . How will the Gophers and Nittany Lions handle their travel and injury issues for their season-turning Big Ten game on Saturday, Nov. 14, in Beaver Stadium? Penn State will miss its star receiver Koby Howard for the seventh straight game to an undisclosed injury. He'll also be joined on the sideline by key backups, defensive end Caleb Bacon and cornerback Jahmir Joseph, both also listed as "out" on the Big Ten's pregame availability report . Nittany Lion starting left tackle Malachi Goodman and backup safety Jeremiah Cooper were listed as "game-time decisions" on the report. Minnesota was even a tougher personnel position: They are missing nine players for Saturday's game, including eight with starting experience. Of course, they're also dealing with an unprecedented travel adventure. Minnesota was one of the few in the Big Ten that got caught in the midst of Friday's four-hour nationwide travel ground stop by the Federal Aviation Authority. Their flight was canceled after the team had boarded in the afternoon. The Gophers, inexplicably, traveled back to campus and could not fly to State College until Saturday morning. They arrived barely seven hours before kickoff. Minnesota arrived carrying a lot of baggage even beyond their unusual same-day arrival. The Gophers and Penn State are both 5-4 but appear to be trending in different directions. While the Nittany Lions broke a four-game losing streak with back-to-back victories, the Gophers are coming off consecutive, excruciating defeats to top-five Indiana and UCLA − games they were tied or led in the fourth quarter. Minnesota owns one of the worst-rated offenses in the nation. They also are now missing their pair of starting defensive tackles, Riley Sunram and Theorin Randle and may be without standout defensive back John Nestor. Penn State's list of unavailable players for the Minnesota game includes Howard, Joseph, Bacon, linebacker Alex Tatsch, defensive ends Max Granville , offensive lineman Will Thompkins, cornerback Tyler Armstead and defensive tackle Alijah Carnell. Leading the league in scoring, Doncic is averaging a career-high 38.6 points a game in leading the Los Angeles Lakers (11-2) to the NBA’s best record. Doncic is averaging an insane 41.8 points, 8.1 rebounds and 7.6 assists in six games during the Lakers’ current seven-game winning streak. item.title: Austria seal top spot with win over Republic of Ireland
item.description: Kalajdzic came off the bench to score the winner for Austria [Getty Images] Republic of Ireland's hopes of securing top spot and automatic promotion to League A were ended by Austria after they suffered a 1-0 defeat in their penultimate Nations League Group B3 game at the Raiffeisen Arena. Substitute Sasa Kalajdzic poked home from a corner to score the winner on 79 minutes as Austria preserved their unbeaten home record, which stretches back to October 2023. The defeat in Linz, Republic of Ireland's second away loss in the group, leaves Heimir Hallgrimsson's side third, a point behind Kosovo, who they face in their final game on Tuesday. A win in that fixture in Dublin would ensure a second-place finish and Republic of Ireland's place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in December. Substitute Kalajdzic scores late winner Austria, who fought back from two goals down to take a point against the Irish in Dublin last month, started well and tested Caoimhin Kelleher just two minutes in as he was forced to get down low to turn Christoph Baumgartner's deflected strike behind. The Irish grew into the game and threatened for the first time on 22 minutes as Troy Parrott connected with Dara O'Shea's delivery from the left, but his acrobatic effort was dealt with by Alexander Schlager. The Real Betis striker went close again soon after when his rising strike from range was tipped over by the goalkeeper. At the other end, Kelleher produced a fine reflex save to push Christoph Lang's half-volley over the crossbar before Michael Gregoritsch, who scored in the 2-2 draw in Dublin, then blasted over. Austria continued to push for the opener in the second half as Gregoritsch's glancing header from a corner landed on the roof of the net and Kelleher then made two good saves to thwart Kevin Danso and Baumgartner. item.title: Dodgers All-Star Free Agent Commanding Widespread Interest
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers free agent Kris Bubic is gathering plenty of interest across MLB, per Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. The Dodgers acquired Bubic at the trade deadline on a rental, sending minor league reliever Carlos Duran the other way. “Free-agent left-hander Kris Bubic, who was traded from the Kansas City Royals to the Los Angeles Dodgers during his second stint on the injured list with elbow soreness, is drawing broad interest from contenders and non-contenders alike, according to a person briefed on his market,” Sammon and Rosenthal wrote. How Did Kris Bubic Perform With the Dodgers? Bubic came to the Dodgers on the injured list after struggling with elbow soreness, so he made just seven appearances out of the bullpen with the team throughout the regular season and postseason. Five of those appearances came in the regular season, where he held opponents scoreless through 4.2 innings pitched while striking out five batters. Bubic didn’t find the same success in the postseason, though, as he allowed two runs through 1.1 innings pitched. Sep 23, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers relief pitcher Kris Bubic (40) delivers against the San Diego Padres in the seventh inning at Dodger Stadium . Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Why is Kris Bubic Such a Popular Free Agent? Bubic, 29, is a starting pitcher by trade, but stepped into the bullpen for the Dodgers to manage his load after his injury. He has a versatile five-pitch arsenal, and he has a solid track record over the past few years despite a few injuries. Before an injury took him out of commission in July 2025, he had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and made the All-Star Game. This season, Bubic had a 3.76 mark through 14 appearances. Free agency is loaded with pitchers this offseason, with Tarik Skubal headlining a class which also consists of players like Freddy Peralta, Nick Martinez and Sonny Gray, but he is one of the top left-handed options available, and is one of the few still yet to turn 30. Spotrac estimates Bubic has a shot to land a four-year, $70 million deal, though he could easily make more than that figure if the his market remains popular. Will the Dodgers Re-Sign Kris Bubic? Bubic is a solid addition to most MLB rosters, but his likelihood of returning to Los Angeles isn’t high. Bubic would likely want to return to an MLB rotation rather than the bullpen, and he will earn more money doing so as well. The Dodgers’ rotation is stacked with talent, making a middling starter signing like Bubic unlikely. Would you bring Kris Bubic back to the Dodgers?

item.title: Nations Championship: Fixtures and standings
item.description: Wales produced the performance of the Nations Championship so far with an historic 35-28 victory over New Zealand at a raucous Principality Stadium on Saturday. In arguably the biggest shock in Test rugby since Japan beat South Africa in the 2015 World Cup, Wales defended heroically to claim their first win over the All Blacks since 1953. The win moved them into fourth place, however, Scotland can move back above Steve Tandy's side if they beat Australia on Sunday. New Zealand might have lost for the first time in the new championship, but they still went top of the standings in the southern hemisphere pool after securing a bonus point. They lead South Africa by one point heading into the final round of group games next Saturday, with the All Blacks facing England and the Springboks taking on Ireland. France ended South Africa's 100% record with a sensational 21-19 victory over the world champions at the Stade de France on Friday. Les Bleus' fourth victory from five pool matches ensure they kept their lead in the northern hemisphere standings. England ran in 13 tries as they thrashed Japan 78-15 to close the gap to France to just one point. Ireland are on the same points total as England after fighting back from a slow start to overwhelm Fiji 43-15. France will be favourites to win the northern group when they face Argentina in the last round but England and Ireland will be hoping they slip up. item.title: How San Antonio game vs. Baylor fits Sean Miller's quest for connection in Texas basketball
item.description: Texas head coach Sean Miller watches his team warm up prior to an NCAA college basketball game against Grambling State in Austin, Texas, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephen Spillman) (Stephen Spillman/Associated Press) AUSTIN - From his corner office desk in one of the University of Texas' most impressive new buildings, Sean Miller can see what many of his predecessors couldn't. Campus, for one thing. In the old days, during the often successful and occasionally captivating eras of Abe Lemons, Tom Penders and Rick Barnes, the Longhorns men's basketball program was headquartered a few blocks away, on the other side of a rise that to most students might as well have been in San Marcos. The now-demolished Erwin Center served its purpose, but it always felt detached from the dormitories and the libraries and the massive stadium that, even more than the iconic school tower, represented what Texas money and know-how could achieve. Generations of basketball coaches tried to bridge that gap. It always proved to be more difficult than it appeared. But when Miller looks at the shrine to football just outside his office window, he eyes the potential for connection. "It's easy for me to embrace," the 57-year-old Miller says, leaning back on a sofa in the state-of-the-art basketball training facility next to the Moody Center, which opened in 2022. "Where I'm at in life, you really see things here that you know don't exist in other places." Other places have programs where the hoops culture is more deeply ingrained. Miller spent most of his life in places like that. He starred as a point guard in the Big East at Pittsburgh, cut his teeth as an assistant on Tobacco Road at North Carolina State, then won lots of games as a head coach throughout two stints at Xavier and one at Arizona. Texas, though, is a place where a basketball lifer like Miller finally can get over the top, and maybe even finish his career, if only he can find a way to channel its abundance of resources toward Final Fours. As a coach, he's never made one. As a program, the Longhorns haven't been to one in almost a quarter-century. To get there, Miller is trying to get the whole place on board. That means extending connections to the new football practice facility across the street, and to the swimming and diving program next door, and to donors in office buildings downtown, and even to chunks of the alumni base in cities like San Antonio. That's one reason why Miller decided to work with Baylor coach Scott Drew to bring Sunday's showdown between the former conference foes to Frost Bank Center. The Longhorns haven't played hoops in San Antonio since packing the Alamodome for an epic 2003 Elite Eight victory over Michigan State that sent them to their only Final Four of the past 79 years. item.title: Red Sox Reportedly Considering Cutting Ties With $60 Million Outfielder
item.description: Boston Red Sox outfielder Kristian Campbell The Boston Red Sox signed Kristian Campbell to an eight-year, $60 million extension after just a handful of games in the big leagues. He was one of their best prospects and looked great through his first month in the big leagues. However, after his first 29 games, he really fell off and was demoted in June 2025. At the time he was both an infielder and outfielder, and in the minor leagues even worked out at first base. However, he has since moved to the outfield full-time, but has not found his way back into the big leagues. Part of that is because of the overcrowded outfield in Boston, but they could clear some of that space up by moving on from Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida, as many experts expect them to do. However, according to CBS Sports's Juliam McWilliams , the Red Sox are considering designating Campbell for assignment. "Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy," wrote McWilliams. "Boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment." Campbell struggled to find his swing even in the minor leagues, but he started to yield better results toward the end of the year. He was the WooSox player of the month in July, slashing .379/.507/.552 with two home runs. In August, he had an .840 OPS, and in five games in September he had seven hits, four walks and five RBIs. He started to look more like a big-league player, but still, there is no clear path for him to play in Boston. The Red Sox have Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield, and now Jake Bauers at designated hitter. item.title: Seahawks elevate two veteran practice squad players ahead of Raiders game
item.description: Although the Seattle Seahawks are set to be without several key starters against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10, they’ll get some much needed depth from two experienced veterans. The Seahawks elevated cornerback Trevon Diggs and offensive tackle Bobby Hart from the practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Raiders, they announced on Saturday . Both players already have suited up for Seattle this season. It marks the third (and final) consecutive elevation for Hart, who’s served as a depth piece behind swing tackle Josh Jones while OT Charles Cross continues to recover from a high ankle sprain he suffered in the team’s Week 7 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. As for Diggs, he’s in line to make his fifth appearance of the year, with his last having come against the Kansas City Chiefs — where the longtime cornerback logged just six defensive snaps. With both Devon Witherspoon and Nehemiah Pritchett healthy, he’s once again unlikely to see a significant role, barring an injury. Despite both having made multiple appearances this season, neither has made a noticeable impact. The veteran lineman played his first three snaps of the season against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 and Diggs has recorded just one tackle across 27 defensive snaps. Given the Seahawks are also poised to be without QB Sam Darnold (quad, ribs), OG Quenton Nelson (knee) and DT Leonard Williams (stinger), it’s unclear why they opted to activate Diggs rather than add depth at a more significant position of need — especially considering there were several players waiting in the wings. While Seattle’s practice squad includes options at each position, none have spent an extended amount of the time with the team. The Seahawks signed OG Cordell Volson on Thursday, DT Cole Brevard two days prior and QB Adrian Martinez on Nov. 4, making it plausible the team didn’t feel any could make as much of an impact as a player like Diggs.
